title: Differential pair with current mirror load

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
Replace the two drain resistors of a differential pair with a PMOS current mirror and you get the classic **mirror-loaded pair**, the first stage of most CMOS op-amps. The diode-connected side, M3, takes M1's current. M4 copies it into the output node, where M2's current is subtracted. A differential input raises one current and lowers the other. The mirror turns M1's change around, so the two changes add at the output instead of cancelling. A single-ended output gets the **full** transconductance \(G_m = g_m\), not half of it.

The output node sees M2's and M4's drains, so \(R_{out} = r_{o2}\parallel r_{o4}\). The gain is \(G_mR_{out}\), the same form as a current-source-loaded CS stage. The circuit is not symmetric, because one side is diode-connected, so half circuits do not apply. Analyse it with \(G_m\) and \(R_{out}\). Common-mode signals are strongly rejected because the mirror's diode side is low-impedance; the reader's estimate is \(\mathrm{CMRR} \approx g_m(r_{o2}\parallel r_{o4})\cdot2g_{m3}R_{SS}\).

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ G_m = g_{m1}, \qquad R_{out} = r_{o2}\parallel r_{o4}, \qquad A_{DM} = g_m(r_{o2}\parallel r_{o4}) \]
\[ \mathrm{CMRR} \approx g_{m1}(r_{o2}\parallel r_{o4})\cdot2g_{m3}R_{SS}, \qquad V_{CM} - V_T \le V_{out} \le V_{DD} - |V_{ov4}| \]

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: Each side carries \(40\ \mu\mathrm{A}\) at \(V_{ov} = 0.16\ \mathrm{V}\), so \(g_m = 0.5\ \mathrm{mS}\). With \(\lambda_n = 0.08\) and \(\lambda_p = 0.125\ \mathrm{V^{-1}}\), \(r_{o2} = 312.5\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\) and \(r_{o4} = 200\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\), so \(R_{out} = 122\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\) and the gain is about 61. Driving 2 pF, it reaches unity gain near \(0.5\ \mathrm{mS}/(2\pi\cdot2\ \mathrm{pF}) \approx 40\ \mathrm{MHz}\).

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Using \(g_m/2\) for \(G_m\), as for a resistor load with a single-ended output.
- Applying half-circuit analysis to the asymmetric load.
- Forgetting that the output swing is limited at both ends.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: As an OTA, this stage is the first stage of an op-amp, where its \(G_m\) and load capacitance set the gain-bandwidth.
